title: Why You Put Things Off, and 3 Ways to Stop

lines: You sit down to work. Ten seconds later, you're holding your phone.
Researchers call this procrastination: putting off something you meant to do, even though you expect the delay to cost you.
A big review pulled together hundreds of results. The pattern was clear: the worse a task feels, the more we put it off.
Some researchers argue it's really about mood. The phone makes you feel better, right now.
But the task is still there. And now there's guilt on top of it.
So here are three things that help.
One: make the start tiny. Open the file and write one line.
A 2025 review found that once we start a task and get stopped, we tend to go back to it.
Two: put the phone out of reach, like in a drawer.
In one study, people who reached their goals simply met fewer temptations. Trying harder to resist was not linked to reaching them.
Three: when you slip, forgive yourself.
In one study, students who forgave themselves for putting off study before one exam put it off less before the next.
So today, pick one task, and do just its tiny first step.
